The root cause of the repeated error is that I attempted to apply the `.apply()` method directly to a list object (`['order_id', 'revenue', ...]`) instead of a pandas Series or DataFrame. This is a syntax error in Python. I must use `.apply()` on a Series, not on a list of column names.

I will now fix the code to correctly extract and inspect the rows with hidden characters by selecting the column as a Series before applying `.apply()`.

function.arguments:
{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Re-load the data to ensure clean state
sales_df = pd.read_csv('/home/musel/Github/research_agent/data/sales.csv')

# Convert 'revenue' to string and inspect for hidden characters using repr
sales_df['revenue_str'] = sales_df['revenue'].astype(str)

# Define pattern to detect invisible Unicode characters
import re
pattern = re.compile(r'\u200b|\xa0|\u200e|\u200f')

# Apply to the string representation of revenue
revenue_repr = sales_df['revenue_str'].apply(repr)
has_hidden = revenue_repr.apply(lambda x: bool(pattern.search(x)))

# Get rows with hidden characters
hidden_rows = sales_df[has_hidden]

# Now correctly extract and display the relevant columns
hidden_rows[['order_id', 'revenue', 'revenue_str']].head()"}
